# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can only act after Deaf identifies the visible wires and Mute communicates the manual’s rule through Deaf. I have no tactile information yet and will not cut anything.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is blue. Three wires in order: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.

Deaf reports display 0, blue light, and wires ordered green, yellow, red. Mute needs these visible details to apply the manual and tell me which position to cut.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light blue; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Please consult manual and tell me the cut position.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured a cycle: symbol one-finger points to V-sign; V-sign points to horns-sign; horns-sign points to one-finger. In short: first maps to second, second maps to third, third maps to first.

Mute has apparently sent Deaf a three-symbol cycle, but that does not yet identify a wire position for me. Since I cannot see gestures, I need Mute’s actual cut instruction relayed verbally by Deaf. I will ask Mute to send one unambiguous gesture corresponding to the required position, and ask Deaf to describe it and any accompanying information.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report of your three-symbol cycle, but I need a definite cut position. Please gesture exactly one of your position symbols for the wire to cut; Deaf, please relay which symbol Mute sends and any manual instruction.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has just gestured only the horns-sign: ?. It is the third symbol in Mute's earlier cycle. I do not know yet whether it means a wire, a control, or an instruction.

The horns sign alone is not a safe instruction because no position mapping has been agreed. I will establish a clear mapping with Mute: one-finger means wire 1, V-sign means wire 2, and horns-sign means wire 3. Mute can then repeat the correct manual-derived answer under that mapping; Deaf can verbally confirm it to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Let us fix a position code: one-finger means wire 1; V-sign means wire 2; horns-sign means wire 3. Using the manual and Deaf's reported bomb details, now send exactly the sign for the wire to cut under this code.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please watch Mute's next single sign and tell me whether it is one-finger, V-sign, or horns-sign. Do not infer a cut yet.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeated the horns-sign again. No new visible bomb changes: display 0, blue light, wires green-yellow-red. Do not operate anything yet; the symbol's meaning remains unconfirmed.

My spoken messages did not reach anyone, so I must use the visible gesture channel. Mute’s repeated horns sign is still not safely grounded as a wire number. I will visibly present the three candidate symbols in a fixed order to both observers, so Deaf and Mute can use that shared ordering for the next confirmation; I will not cut.

``` 
gesture(symbols=["☝","✌","🤘"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has now repeated ? three times total. I saw your gesture sequence: one-finger, V-sign, then rock-sign. Please say aloud what physical parts or choices your sequence represents, if you can; do not operate yet.

Deaf confirms that Mute consistently selects the rock/horns sign, but neither of us has a confirmed convention tying that sign to wire 1, 2, or 3. My attempted speech cannot reach either monkey, so I cannot clarify it verbally. I will not operate while the mapping remains ambiguous.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has repeated ? again, now four times total. I have just given Mute the full visible state so they can apply the manual. Do not operate yet.

Mute has repeatedly and consistently indicated the same third symbol after receiving the full visible state. Deaf identifies it as the horns/rock sign, the third item in the communicated three-sign cycle. The only actionable interpretation is wire position 3, so I will cut wire 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
